introducoes.uso: FeatherDocs is a document editor that runs entirely on your machine: no account, no login, none of your text leaves it. Here is how to use each part, from typing and formatting to tables, page setup and files. Follow in order with the arrow, or pick a topic in the side menu.
introducoes.atalhos: The keys that get things done faster. All of them work with the cursor in the text; the file ones work anywhere in the window.

corpo: Click the page and type: text appears where the cursor blinks. Enter starts a new paragraph; Backspace joins it to the previous one.
• Drag the mouse (or use Shift + arrows) to select, even across paragraphs.
• Double-click selects the word; triple-click, the paragraph.
• Ctrl+Z undoes and Ctrl+Y redoes.
Commands are in the ribbon at the top and in the menus (File, Edit, View…). Double-clicking a ribbon tab minimizes it.
The Home button in the corner goes back to the start page; the document stays open and you return with "Back to the document".
Select the text and use the ribbon (Home → Font) or the keyboard. With no selection, the formatting applies to what you type next.
• Bold Ctrl+B, italic Ctrl+I, underline Ctrl+U, code Ctrl+E, strikethrough Ctrl+Shift+X.
• Repeating the command on an already formatted selection removes the formatting.
Tip: typing # and a space at the start of a line makes a heading (## is level 2, and so on); "- " makes a list, "1. " a numbered list, "> " a quote, "---" a horizontal line.

As you type, quotes become curly quotes (“ ”), -- becomes an em dash (—), ... becomes an ellipsis (…) and sentences start with a capital letter. Ctrl+Z right after undoes just the correction; Review → Correct as you type turns it off.
Right-click a word to see synonyms; picking one replaces the word (keeping the capital letter).
Spell check also underlines repeated words ("the the"), double spaces and a space before a comma or period; right-click to fix it.

In Portuguese text it also catches some common usage errors: “houveram” (should be “houve”), “fazem dois anos” (“faz”), “à partir” (“a partir”), “entre eu e” (“entre mim e”), “para mim fazer” (“para eu fazer”) and “há dez anos atrás” (“há dez anos”).

Text in another language (an abstract, a quote in English): select it and choose Review → Language. That text is then checked with the dictionary of its language (Portuguese, English and Spanish are included; other languages are just not underlined), and the language goes with it to .docx. Text with no language set follows the document, or the interface language.
A whole document in one language (a letter in Spanish): Review → Language → Whole document. It applies to all text without its own language; a new document already starts in the interface language.
Check also points out sentences that are too long (more than 45 words), which run past three lines and tire the reader: clicking one selects it so you can split it in two.

The Review panel also shows the reading time (200 words a minute) and the speaking time (130 a minute): handy when preparing a ten-minute talk. With text selected, it counts only the selection. The goal (Review → Word goal…) can be in words, in characters with spaces (as essays and calls for papers ask) or both: the bottom bar counts them and turns red when you go over.
Before sending, Review → Check lists what is still open: broken cross-references, citations without a source, open comments, suggested changes and unknown words. Clicking an item takes you there.

Academic papers: in the Check panel, turn on ABNT rules. The list then flags paper other than A4, margins other than 3 / 2 / 2 / 3 cm, body paragraphs not in 12 pt or not at 1.5 spacing, and long quotes (over three lines) without the 4 cm indent. It only points things out: check your school's guide, which sometimes changes a rule.
The paragraph style is under Home → Styles (Normal, Heading 1 to 3, and more under the ▾ button) or Format → Paragraph styles. Ctrl+Alt+0 to 6 also switch it: 0 is normal text, 1 to 6 are headings.
• Bulleted list: Ctrl+Shift+8. Numbered list: Ctrl+Shift+7. Repeating the style undoes the list.
• Tab goes one level down in a list and Shift+Tab goes up.
• Insert → Table of contents adds an index that FeatherDocs keeps up to date with the headings.
The Outline button (View) opens a panel with the document's headings; clicking one jumps there.
• Next to each heading you see the words in its section. Drag the ⋮ handle to the left of a heading to move the whole section (subheadings and text included) somewhere else.
• Alt+Shift+↑ and Alt+Shift+↓ move the paragraph at the cursor (or the selected paragraphs) up and down.

• Putting a list in alphabetical order: select the paragraphs or items and click Sort A to Z (Home → Paragraph); in the classic menu, Format → Sort paragraphs also has Z to A. Capitals and accents are ignored, “item 2” comes before “item 10” and empty lines go to the end. One Ctrl+Z undoes it. A list with sub-items is sorted one level at a time, and nothing is sorted in Suggest mode.
Insert → Table creates a table with the cursor in the first cell. Tab moves to the next cell and, in the last one, adds a row.

Right-click a table → Open in FeatherSheet: a copy of the table opens as a spreadsheet (FeatherSheet must be installed). The document does not change; to bring numbers back, copy them in the spreadsheet and paste inside the table.
Copying a range from a spreadsheet (FeatherSheet, Excel, LibreOffice) and pasting it makes a table; pasted inside a table, it fills the cells from the cursor. Ctrl+Shift+V pastes it as text.
Layout → Paper switches between A4 and Letter; Layout → Margins offers Normal (2.54 cm), Narrow (1.27 cm), Moderate, Wide and ABNT.
Layout → Breaks inserts page, column, text wrapping (Shift+Enter) and section breaks (next page, continuous, even page and odd page).
FeatherDocs refuses a margin that leaves less than 100 pt (about 3.5 cm) of width for the text.
View → Zoom (or Ctrl + mouse wheel) changes the size of the page on screen without changing the document.
Ctrl+G (Edit → Go to page) jumps to a page by its number and puts the cursor at its start.
FeatherDocs' own format is .fdoz. It also opens Markdown (.md), LaTeX (.tex) and Word (.docx).
• File → Save (Ctrl+S) and Save as (Ctrl+Shift+S) write .fdoz. In the browser, the file is downloaded.
• File → Export writes Markdown or LaTeX.
• The window title shows a dot (•) when there are unsaved changes; the footer says "Saved" or "Not saved".
• Files → Print (Ctrl+P) shows on the left how each sheet will come out, watermark included; the printer, copies and pages are on the right. Ctrl+Shift+P exports the PDF.
• When you reopen a document, the cursor goes back to the paragraph where you stopped.

• A document you write over and over (the weekly memo, the monthly report): Files → Save as template. It shows on the start page under New, and opening it always creates a new document, never overwriting the template. The X on the card removes it.

• Word forms (.docx with fields): click a box to tick or clear it; click a list to pick an option, or a date to type it (or use Today). In a text field the sample text is selected and goes away as you type. Save as .docx and Word reads what you filled in.

• To build a form: Insert → Form puts a check box, a list (options separated by semicolons), a date or a text field at the cursor. Give the field a name: it shows when filling it in and to the AI assistant.
Everything stays on your computer: FeatherDocs has no account, cloud or telemetry.
The gear (at the top of the window) opens Settings: theme (automatic, light or dark), accent color and language.
Theme, color and language apply right away.

teclas.palavra: Go to the previous or next word
teclas.linha: Start and end of the line
teclas.documento: Start and end of the document
teclas.apagar: Delete backward and forward (with Ctrl, a word)
teclas.tab: Go down or up a list level; move between table cells
teclas.moverParagrafo: Move the paragraph up or down
teclas.fechar: Close Settings or leave the start page
